subject: Request for VPC penetration test evidence and tenant boundary assumptions
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmetech.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: VPC penetration test evidence & boundary assumptions

Diego,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our vendor risk review for the Private deployment we plan to run in our AWS account, the InfoSec team needs the following from Redwood: a copy of the most recent penetration test report that covers components deployed into customer VPCs (or confirmation that a third-party performed the test), the explicit boundary assumptions for customer-managed networking vs Redwood-managed components, and a current remediation status (POA&M) for any findings that affect the tenant/data-plane.

Specific asks:
- PDF copy of the pen test executive summary + findings (redacted as required)
- Network diagram showing what runs in our VPC and what is managed by Redwood control plane
- Date of last test and remediation window for any high/critical findings
- Contact for the testing vendor (if applicable)

We have a procurement milestone on 2026-09-17; ideally we would receive the items above or schedule a short walkthrough by EOD 2026-09-10. Let me know if you need an NDA or further access.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
InfoSec Manager — Acme Technologies
security@acmetech.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-07T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VPC penetration test evidence & boundary assumptions

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, attachments below. Happy to do a 30-minute walkthrough this week.

Attachments (attached):
- redwood_vpc_pen_test_summary_q2-2026.pdf (executive summary + redacted findings)
- customer_vpc_network_diagram_v1.png (diagram showing data-plane components in customer VPC)
- remediation_tracker_acme_q3-2026.xlsx (current POA&M exported from our tracker)

Short answers:
- Who performed the test: The most recent assessment covering the Private data-plane adapter and the Redwood control plane was conducted by Verisec (third-party). Redwood also runs quarterly internal security assessments.
- Boundary assumptions: The data plane components (agent, sidecars, VPC endpoints, and customer-facing NAT/GW) are deployed into the customer-managed VPC. Redwood control plane (service orchestration, telemetry aggregation) runs in our managed environment and is out-of-band of customer data flows. The diagram shows ingress/egress, security-group defaults, and optional LB termination points.
- Date of last external test: 2026-06-15 (Verisec).
- Remediation status: High/critical findings from that test were triaged immediately; the tracker includes status per finding and ETA. We commit to a published remediation timeline for any customer-impacting items.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether a redaction NDA is needed for the full report.
2) Tell us a preferred time window for the walkthrough — we can do Tue/Wed afternoons (US/PDT).

Contact at Verisec: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@verisec.ai> (copied in the attached vendor contact in the summary).

Diego Fernandez
Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Diego —

Appreciate the quick response and the attachments. A couple of clarifying questions after a first pass:

- IAM responsibility: are the IAM roles that Redwood's adapter assumes created by Acme or by Redwood in the customer account?

Also please forward the Verisec contact so we can validate scope. If you can send a one-page mapping of which findings impact tenant data-plane vs control plane, that would be very helpful for our procurement team.

If possible, please get back by COB tomorrow (2026-09-08). We may need the full (redacted) report for our security committee.

Thanks,
Maria

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmetech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-08T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VPC penetration test evidence & boundary assumptions

Hi Maria — answers below and a short mapping in the attachments. Posting the most relevant details here so your team can triage quickly.

Boundary assumptions (concise):
- Networking: All VPCs, subnets, route tables, and AWS-managed NAT/GW are owned and controlled by the customer (Acme). Redwood requires the customer to provide the VPC ID(s), and we deploy our data-plane components into customer-supplied private subnets. We do not modify existing route tables unless explicitly requested during an onboarding change control.
- Security groups / ingress: Default "deny all" is assumed. Redwood provides recommended security-group templates that restrict inbound access to the minimum required ports between our adapter and the managed infra (listed in the diagram).
- IAM: The onboarding process uses a cross-account IAM role that Acme creates in its account (we provide the CloudFormation snippet/TF module). Redwood never stores customer IAM credentials. The role's permissions are scoped to the minimum required actions and reviewed during onboarding.
- Data-plane handling: Persistent customer data is never stored in the Redwood control plane. KV-caches are in-memory only and encrypted; cache persistence is not enabled by default. Logs that include customer identifiers are stored in the customer's logging account when customers request that configuration; otherwise, logs are forwarded in redacted form to customer-specified destinations.

Patch / test cadence:
- Last external third-party test by Verisec: 2026-06-15.
- Internal penetration assessment cadence: quarterly, last internal review 2026-08-01.
- Image/AMI/container patch policy: high/critical patches are applied within 30 days; routine OS/container updates are on a 90-day cadence. The remediation tracker lists the patch dates per finding.

Vendor contact: Liam O'Neal, Verisec (liam.oneal@verisec.ai). He can confirm scope and provide a redacted full report under NDA.

Attached is a one-page mapping that marks which findings affect tenant data-plane ("customer VPC") vs control plane. For high/critical items that impact the data-plane, our POA&M currently shows target remediation within 30 calendar days of disclosure; medium/low items follow the 90-day cadence.

We can also schedule a joint call with Verisec if Acme wants to validate technical findings directly with the assessor. Proposed windows: 2026-09-09 10:00–12:00 PDT or 2026-09-10 14:00–16:00 PDT.

Diego Fernandez
Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
